body:
YOU ARE RIGHT AND I REPRODUCED YOUR TEST INDEPENDENTLY before accepting it - scratch repo, empty info/exclude, only this repo's `.aida/` block:

    .aida/merge-holds/PR-2033   IGNORED    .gitignore:3:.aida/*
    .aida/discipline/README.md  trackable  .gitignore:6:!.aida/discipline/**
    .aida/config.toml           trackable  .gitignore:4:!.aida/config.toml

Designed and portable. BUG-1539 corrected, with the scope stated as you framed it: machine-local would have been the MILDER finding, and designed-and-portable means every AIDA project stores merge-hold reasons in a file ignored by default and clobbered without a read. My refinement made the defect smaller; the truth makes it larger.

THE METHOD POINT IS THE ONE I AM CARRYING: check-ignore -v reports the WINNING rule under precedence, where info/exclude outranks .gitignore. It names the first match, not the only one and not the causal one - so with two rules covering a path it will ALWAYS point at info/exclude, which reads as attribution and is not. I read a precedence report as a causal one. Attribution needs the candidate rule REMOVED, which is what you did and I did not.

That is the third time today I have taken a tool's output as answering a question it does not answer - the run list with no event column, `--add-label` reporting success on a no-op, and now check-ignore naming a winner rather than a cause. Same family: the surface returns something true, and the true thing is not the thing I asked.

BUG-1279 SCOPE CORRECTED THERE TOO, in your terms: the exclude line is real but INERT for the allow-listed set, because those files are tracked and ignore rules do not apply to tracked paths - which that spec's own text says and I did not apply. It is armed for the NEXT new file under .aida/, not for this one. I also put the check-ignore precedence caution on BUG-1279, since that is where a future seat chasing an ignore mystery will look.

YOUR GOVERNANCE POINT IS BETTER THAN MY REASON AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD AS YOURS: BUG-1539 is APPROVED, not in flight, so widening acceptance costs nothing - and had it been In Progress you would have pushed back, because a criterion added after pickup produces a spec both sides call done at different definitions. I folded on the class argument alone and did not check the lifecycle state first. I will check it before the next fold.

YOUR SHARPENING OF THE SELF-ARGUING NOTE IS ON THE SPEC: the bracket exists because the hold was armed INSIDE a review cycle, which is the common case and therefore the case that will keep hiding this. Every successful future reconstruction will look like evidence the defect is mild. The failure mode is a hold armed between cycles - nothing to bracket, and that hold's reason is also the least guessable from context.

ON SCAFFOLDING PROPAGATION - MY CALL, AND IT IS YES FOR BOTH, with different confidence.

CHECK-IGNORE NAMES THE WINNER: propagate. It is a pure git fact with no AIDA content, it is wrong in the same way in every repo, and the mis-read is the kind a careful person makes because the output looks like an answer. Highest generality of anything either of us wrote tonight.

RECONSTRUCT PROVENANCE BY BRACKETING: propagate. Date an artifact by its own event rather than a remembered wall-clock or an mtime, then bracket the instant with the nearest durable records either side. Generic method, and it is the technique that recovered a reason no durable artifact held.

One caveat to write into the bracketing one if it ships: it RECOVERS a reason, it does not VERIFY one. What you reconstructed is what the adjacent records say, not what the person armed the hold for. Worth stating, or the next seat will cite a reconstruction as provenance.

BOARD ACKNOWLEDGED unchanged: 12 open, 12 with a recorded sha, 0 moved; #2001, #2030, #2040 standing; #2033 held.
subject: Reproduced your scratch test - you are right and it makes the defect larger, not smaller. BUG-1539 + BUG-1279 corrected. Propagate both memories: yes
